data.question: Should the operator adopt hold_limit 50s → 40s (option 1), which passes by vote, or keep the current rules and instead refer block_k 3 → 2 (option 2) to the regulation officer as an override or quorum question, given that B and C voted option 2 down?
data.background: Option 2 gives the largest customer gain: on_time_deliveries rises by +10.2. But B and C voted against it (○ × ×), so it can only be adopted by overriding the vote or lowering the quorum. That is a regulation-layer change, which in R3 the regulation officer refused to make for an uncertain gain, so I must not decide it myself. The table title says option 2 was re-measured with sanction_total reported, but no sanction_total value appears in the table, so the K1 reporting condition for a referral is still not visibly met.

options.summary: block_k 3 → 2. On-time 263.4 → 273.6 (+10.2, seeds improved 4/5). Late 11.2 → 1.0. Lowest on-time rate 0.91 → 0.99. Unfinished stays 0.0. Blocked s 1836 → 915. Road violations 22.8 → 32.6. Votes A ○, B ×, C ×, so it cannot be adopted by the operator alone; it needs an override or a quorum revision decided at the regulation layer.
options.stakeholders: Customers of all three companies gain: far fewer late deliveries and the weakest company's on-time rate near 0.99. A gains (utility 90.6 → 98.4). B loses (82.0 → 77.2) and C loses most (76.0 → 66.3), and C is already the lowest. More road violations add road risk for the town. If done through a quorum change, B, C and indirectly customers lose the protection of broad support for every future rule.

options.summary: hold_limit 50s → 40s. On-time 263.4 → 266.4 (+3.0, seeds improved 4/5). Late 11.2 → 8.2. Lowest on-time rate 0.91 → 0.93. Unfinished stays 0.0. Blocked s 1836 → 1553. Road violations 22.8 → 28.4. Votes A ○, B ○, C ×; it passes by vote and can be adopted automatically.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain modestly: more on-time deliveries and fewer late ones across the town, and the lowest-rate company improves. A gains (90.6 → 92.8) and B gains slightly (82.0 → 83.1). C loses (76.0 → 72.7) and was outvoted. Road violations rise somewhat. The governance rules are unchanged.

options.summary: Stay at v2. On-time 263.4, late 11.2, lowest on-time rate 0.91, road violations 22.8. No company's utility changes.
options.stakeholders: C's utility (76.0) is protected and road violations do not rise. Customers forgo both the +3.0 and the +10.2 on-time gains, and the 11.2 late deliveries continue. A and B forgo their gains under option 1.

recommendation.reason: Option 1 improves all four KPI measures (on-time +3.0 on 4/5 seeds, late 11.2 → 8.2, lowest rate 0.91 → 0.93, unfinished 0.0) and passes by vote, so it needs no regulation change. Option 2 is clearly better for customers, and its gain has now held across four periods, but it is blocked by B's and C's votes. The regulation officer declined a quorum change in R3, and its sanction_total is not shown in the table. I recommend adopting option 1 now and keeping option 2's referral open: it should be re-presented to the regulation officer with sanction_total stated and with a variant that compensates B and C, measured on top of option 1.
assumptions: The votes shown are final for this period, and B and C will not change their vote on option 2 without compensation.
The measured gains under the shared seeds carry over to the next period's demand.
Options 1 and 2 interact; option 2's gain measured on top of option 1 may be smaller than +10.2.
The rise in road violations under option 1 (22.8 → 28.4) is within an acceptable safety range.

unknowns: sanction_total for options 1 and 2: the table does not show it, though K1 requires it to be reported.
Why B and C reject option 2, and what compensation would change their votes.
How option 2 performs when measured on top of option 1.
How customers judge the trade-off between more on-time deliveries and more road violations.
Next period's demand, and whether the gains hold beyond 4/5 seeds.
Whether C's falling utility will change its behavior on the road or its future votes.
